standfirst: Every feature the Bornaviridae module declares, the profiles behind it, and what fraction of its own collection each one recovers. The family is six proteins — N, X, P, M, G and L — plus the two furin products of the glycoprotein and two glycoprotein-derived ORFs that only one genus carries. Built 17–18 November 2026; every citation on this page is model-proposed and awaits a curator.

modules.Bornaviridae: One module for the whole family. Gene content is identical in Orthobornavirus, Carbovirus, Cultervirus and Cartilovirus; only the order differs (M and G are transposed outside Orthobornavirus, and Cartilovirus inserts two extra ORFs), and order does not enter a profile. 16 reference contigs route 100% of the 218 near-complete genomes.

why.N: The 38/39 kDa nucleocapsid doublet, the most abundant protein in infected cells (PMID 9188580). The 38 kDa alternative-initiation isoform is deliberately not a feature: it is an exact C-terminal substring of the 39 kDa form, nothing in BV-BRC deposits it, and the second in-frame Met sits at residue 14 in only 69 of 129 collection members, so no fixed offset is derivable.
why.X: The non-structural X protein (p10), encoded by an ORF overlapping the 5' end of P and a negative regulator of polymerase activity (PMID 15992626). Nine of its eighteen profiles exist only because the coverage run found X uncalled in every non-Orthobornavirus genus; a tenth was recovered by ORF-calling a genome that deposits no X at all.
why.P: The polymerase cofactor p24 (PMID 9268312). Four truncated deposits that begin 19-40 residues inside the protein were dropped before the profiles were built, after check_met_start flagged a cluster whose members start with Gly.
why.M: Matrix protein; the crystal structure shows a tetramer that binds single-stranded RNA (PMID 19237566).
why.G: The envelope glycoprotein precursor p57, glycosylated to gp94 and cleaved by furin (PMID 9557754).
why.G_N: The N-terminal furin product. It retains the signal peptide, because no mature N-terminus has ever been determined for a bornavirus glycoprotein and this build will not ship a prediction as if it were a measurement.
why.G_C: The C-terminal furin product, residues 250-503 of the BoDV-1 precursor. It carries the membrane anchor and runs to the precursor's own stop, so only its N-terminus is a cleaved end.
why.L: The 190 kDa polymerase (PMID 10756058). In Orthobornavirus it is a two-exon protein whose first exon contributes five or six residues, and it is collinear in the other three genera; the limit that follows is stated in the coverage audit rather than hidden.
why.VP1: Cartilovirus only: an ancient duplication of the glycoprotein gene (PMID 38028148). One genome exists in the whole of BV-BRC, so this is a single-sequence profile and its bit cutoff was measured, not defaulted.
why.VP2: Cartilovirus only: a second duplication, 44% identical to Vp1 (PMID 38028148). Also a single-sequence profile.

derived: G_N and G_C have no collection of their own. Nothing in BV-BRC is annotated as a mature bornavirus glycoprotein, so both products were cut out of the G collection at the furin site rather than collected. Richt 1998 (PMID 9557754) places that site after the arginine at position 249 of the 503 aa BoDV-1 precursor; the derivation here finds the single R-X-[K/R]-R match in the 40-62% window and extends it through the basic run, which reproduces residue 249 exactly and generalises to every genus.
gaps: The one protein this module cannot reproduce exactly is the orthobornavirus L N-terminus, and the reason is biological rather than a tuning failure: five or six of its residues come from a separate exon.
Vp1 and Vp2 rest on one genome each, which is every Cartilovirus genome that exists in BV-BRC. Their profiles recall that genome and nothing else is available to test them on.
